query: How is Aurora retrieval evaluated and what release criteria are used?

chunks.text: The Aurora retrieval stack combines lexical BM25 retrieval with a vector index. The result merger deduplicates candidates before reranking.
Aurora is evaluated with Recall at five, mean reciprocal rank, and answer citation coverage on a manually labeled question set.
The benchmark compares Aurora against a lexical-only baseline on the same held-out questions. It reports recall and MRR.
Aurora is evaluated with Recall at five, mean reciprocal rank, and answer citation coverage on a manually labeled question set.
In version two, the Aurora team updated the CSS grid spacing, icons, and light mode palette in the dashboard.
Aurora caches metadata locally and records a timestamp with every retrieved source. Queries are not uploaded by this demo.
The retrieval service budget allocates thirty milliseconds for lexical search and fifty milliseconds for reranking on its internal sample.
The kitchen inventory includes rice, tomatoes, lentils and cumin for next week.
The release gate requires at least ninety percent citation coverage and Recall at five above eighty percent on the held-out set.
Aurora uses a hybrid search pipeline and evaluates retrieval with Recall at five and mean reciprocal rank.
